literal: Among all those who stood outside virtue, fools than those who stood at another man's gate there are not.
translation: Among all those who stand outside the bounds of virtue, there are no greater fools than those who stand at another man's door.
modern: அறத்தை விட்டு விலகி பாவம் செய்தவர்கள் அனைவரிலும், மற்றொருவனின் வீட்டு வாசலில் சென்று நிற்பவர்களை விடப் பெரிய முட்டாள்கள் யாருமில்லை.
explanation: This couplet compares different types of wrongdoers to highlight the sheer foolishness of coveting another man's wife. The word 'அறன்கடை' refers to standing outside moral boundaries, encompassing all those who commit sins. 'பிறன்கடை' literally means another man's gate, painting a vivid picture of a man lurking outside his neighbor's house with illicit intentions. By stating that there are no greater fools than these men, the text emphasizes that adultery is not just a moral failing, but an act of supreme stupidity.
